fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. "A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool." A rebuke on one side and a hundred lashes on the other. And it's the rebuke that cuts deeper into the man of discernment. I think that's because he actually listens, and the words land.

Right, baker. "Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous—both are detestable to the LORD." He names both verdicts. The word is both, and avoiding just one isn't what the verse says. A judge can't pick a favorite way to get it wrong.

Wise from a broken spirit would be a nice twist, but this verse doesn't go there. It says "A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones." That's a dry, brittle picture, like a cookie left in the oven way too long. I've been that cookie, baker. Give me the joyful heart every time.
